core.title: One architectural decision lives in exactly one ADR file
core.given: A docs corpus that records architectural decisions as ADRs in a dedicated decisions directory
core.when: You plan, author or review an architectural decision, or review the ADR corpus
core.then: Record each architectural decision in exactly one ADR file that declares the decision. Do not split or duplicate it across ADR files, and do not put it in the registry.
prefer: Write a new decision as its own ADR file following the stack's decision-record naming, carrying the stack's required decision-record header, and declaring the decision with the stack's decision-declaration construct, then regenerate the registry.
avoid: Typing decision content into the decision registry. It belongs in an ADR file that declares the decision. The registry holds references to decisions, never the decisions themselves.
core.why: One decision in ONE ADR file is what makes the registry a navigable set with a single source of truth per decision (spec 2 §6). An exact, regenerated listing still cannot repair a decision scattered across files.
evidence: Each architectural decision in the plan or corpus maps to exactly one ADR file that declares the decision, and the registry holds only references.
verification: Judged by a reviewer or LLM: whether decision content is split across ADR files, duplicated, or held outside an ADR file is read from the corpus content; it is not machine-checked.
The stack's automated docs check covers registry drift only; it cannot detect a decision that is split or duplicated across ADR files, so an exact registry listing does not clear this rule.
What counts as an ADR — its decisions directory, record file naming, required record-header attributes and decision-declaration construct — is supplied by the profile, not hardcoded by the check.

values: decision content split across ADR files, duplicated in several ADR files, or held outside an ADR file

fires: A plan records one architectural decision across two or more ADR files (for example, the choice in one and its rationale in another, or the same decision restated in two ADRs).
A decision's content (choice, rationale) is written into the decision registry or another non-ADR document instead of an ADR file that declares the decision.
A docs review finds an existing decision that is split or duplicated across ADR files, even though the registry listing matches the ADR set exactly.
doesNotFire: Several ADR files that each record a distinct decision, even when their decision declarations target the same architecture node.
The registry holds one reference per ADR, with no decision content.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the decisions corpus (decision records and their registry) lives; the core's given and activation scope resolve to this directory.
The file-name pattern of one decision record, used when the core says 'as its own ADR file following the stack's decision-record naming'.
The derived registry file that indexes the decision records and must hold references only, never decision content.

The required record-header attributes of every decision record (its record metadata: identifier, status, date), besides the decision declaration; the core's 'carrying the stack's required decision-record header' and the record definition in verification resolve to it.
The construct by which a decision record declares the architectural decision it records; the core's 'declares the decision' resolves to it.

proposedKeys.meaning: Directory that holds the architecture decision records and their derived registry.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roles.<role>.path admits only the ten code/test roles (no documentation role), and neither roots nor layout has any docs-corpus key.

proposedKeys.meaning: File-name pattern of one architecture decision record under the decisions directory.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.<file_kind> lists file-kind suffixes and its params have no decision-record kind; layout has per-artifact patterns (layout.plan_item) but none for decision records.

proposedKeys.meaning: The derived registry file that indexes the decision records.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key names any registry or index artifact of a docs corpus.

proposedKeys.meaning: The required record-header attributes of every decision record (record metadata: identifier, status, date), besides the decision declaration.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group has no key for a document template's required attributes; urn.declaration covers plan-artifact URNs and urn.binding.<artifact> covers source/test bindings, and neither describes a decision record's header metadata.

proposedKeys.meaning: The construct by which a decision record declares the architectural decision it records.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.binding.<artifact> binds source and test files to URNs; no idiom key covers a decision record's declaration of its decision.

bunOnly.text: docs_capability checks registry drift only and cannot detect a decision that is split or duplicated across ADR files.
bunOnly.reason: docs_capability is this stack's validator id; per the vocabulary, detector/validator ids of a single rule are realization details, and the core's verification names the check generically (automated registry-drift check).

bunOnly.text: ADR = a document at `docs/architecture/decisions/adr-YYYYMMDD-NNN-<slug>.adoc` declaring `:adr-id:`, `:status:`, `:date:` and `:decides:`.
bunOnly.reason: The concrete AsciiDoc syntax of the term definition stays in the Bun realization; every slot it pins (directory, file pattern, record-header attributes, decision declaration) is profiled, so the core's record definition in verification instantiates it fully for another stack.

bunOnly.text: Write a new decision as its own `adr-YYYYMMDD-NNN-<slug>.adoc` with `:adr-id:`, `:status:`, `:date:` and `:decides:`
bunOnly.reason: The literal file pattern and AsciiDoc attribute names are the Bun values of the profiled record-naming, record-header and decision-declaration keys; the concrete syntax stays in the reference example, while the neutral requirement covers all of it through those slots.

classification.note: The path docs/architecture/decisions is the profile's decisions directory; the core keeps only 'a docs corpus with a dedicated decisions directory'.

'declares :decides:' becomes 'declares the decision', with the AsciiDoc attribute supplied by the profile's decision-declaration construct. The three sentences state one obligation, kept intact (no condition dropped, none added).
Neutral as written; the spec 2 §6 citation is a methodology reference, not a stack mechanism.

The core keeps the full shape (own record per decision, with the stack's record naming, required record header and decision declaration, then regenerate the registry); naming, header attributes and declaration come from the profile, so no part of the Bun guidance is lost; the literal AsciiDoc syntax stays Bun-only.
decisions/index.adoc becomes the profile's registry file; ':decides:' becomes the declaration construct; the reference-only rule for the registry is kept.
Same substitutions as then/avoid: 'with :decides:' -> 'declares the decision', 'index.adoc' -> 'the registry'.
'Judged by a reviewer or LLM' and the registry-drift limitation are neutral verification scope; 'docs_capability' is the stack's validator id, which is a realization detail, not a profile key.

The ADR term definition pins path, pattern, record-header attributes and the declaration construct; each slot is profiled, and the core's verification states that the record definition comes from the profile; the concrete AsciiDoc syntax remains the realization's.
Per-rule severity (2) belongs to core verification. bun.json states no disposition, so the core adds none — only 'Severity 2.' is carried.
path_glob is not in the closed fact vocabulary; re-expressed as a file_kind fact whose values resolve through the profile keys to the same two globs (ADR files plus the registry).

Operation fact kept verbatim. Its note (this fact alone is not required; the change fact also applies when an existing corpus is reviewed) is activation semantics preserved by keeping both facts and the third fires example.
The change values are neutral and kept; the note's 'Registry drift checks cannot see it' becomes a core verification exclusion.

neutralityNotes: The term 'ADR' is kept: it names a stack-neutral documentation practice (architecture decision record), not a runtime, framework or file format. The decisions-corpus location, ADR file naming, registry file, the required record-header attributes (:adr-id:, :status:, :date:) and the :decides: declaration had no keys in the closed vocabulary, so five keys are proposed (layout.decisions_dir, layout.adr_file, layout.adr_registry, idiom.decision_record_header, idiom.decision_declaration); until the owner approves them, a second stack cannot fully instantiate this core from the closed vocabulary alone. The record-header key keeps the document-template idiom profiled rather than bunOnly, so another stack can supply equivalent record metadata; only the concrete AsciiDoc syntax stays in the Bun realization. The validator id (docs_capability) remains bunOnly as a realization detail. activation.facts[0].path_glob was re-expressed as the closed-vocabulary file_kind fact; its exact globs are recovered from the proposed profile keys. Per-rule severity (2) is carried in core verification; bun.json declares no disposition, so the core deliberately states none. The spec 2 §6 citation is retained as a methodology reference.
